headline: Western Russia: Zelenskyy: Russia strikes area between Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra and monastery with ballistic missile carrying cluster warhead
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Western Russia: Zelenskyy: Russia strikes area between Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra and monastery with ballistic missile carrying cluster warhead.
- Africa: Ukraine: At least 9 people were killed in Russian attacks over the past 24 hours.
- South Asia: Saudis intercept more drones as conflict with Houthis spirals.

Full breakdown follows.

- Military Times, one hour ago: US Army long-range fires make a splash on the frontline with China.
The U.S. Army has been upgrading its missiles and rocket artillery, largely in response to China's missile arsenal.

Eligable lieutenants and lieutenant commanders in the explosive ordnance disposal field are eligible for up to $100,000 in retention bonuses.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Holness blasts ‘two-mouth people’, defends JCF.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 11 hours ago: Holness blasts ‘two-mouth people’, defends JCF.
Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness yesterday launched a blistering attack on critics of law enforcement, blasting “two-mouth people” while declaring his unwavering support for the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF). Holness comments come amid public debate over last Friday’s deadly gun battle in Sligoville, St Catherine. Speaking at a handover ceremony for the East Palms housing development in Kingston Central, Holness said state intervention was bringing positive changes to inner-city communities.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

A Russian attack on a market in Lozova, Kharkiv Oblast, has killed two people and injured 34; emergency crews are working at the scene.

- Balkan Insight, 10 hours ago: Acquittal Fuels Doubts over Transfer of Bosnian War Crimes Cases to Serbia.
While a court in Bosnia and Herzegovina has sentenced 13 people to a combined total of more than 180 years in prison for the killing of Bosniak civilians in two villages during the 1992-95 war, the acquittal of two others by a court in Belgrade has raised further doubts about the merit of transferring war crimes cases from Sarajevo to Belgrade.

The attack on Monday also forced about 8,000 people to flee, prompting condemnation from the United Nations and the UK.

Ultimately, the court awarded the Rubys $27,000, with $20,000 for invasion of privacy. However, the appeals court overturned the privacy ruling, necessitating further proceedings and adjusting the damages for tree removal.

The couple’s relationship had deteriorated, leading to frequent quarrels about her phone conversations. On October 10, Irfaj killed Ruksana with a stone and concealed her body in a stormwater drain. Police discovered her body three days later and identified her after public inquiries.

Attendees praised Haines for her compassion, support for young people and ability to bring people together across political divides. One community member said Haines was reasonable, fair and considerate and 'listened to everybody'.
